messages:
maya: Heads-up — planning a small release tonight during the 23:00-01:00 PT change window. Goal: publish Python canary v1.8.0-canary, then TypeScript v2.3.0-canary. Also want to land deprecation wording for the legacy sync client.

kyle: SGTM. I prefer staggered: py -> smoke -> ts. avoids cross-language churn.

release-manager: +1. Staggered publish. If py smoke fails we hold ts and either rollback or cut a patch. Need explicit pinning plan for monorepo examples and quick rollback cmds.

maya: Plan: 1) publish py canary to TestPyPI + tag on pypi as canary 2) run smoke and e2e on dedicated infra 3) if green, publish ts canary to npm dist-tag canary 4) run client smoke.

sam: Can we also pin the examples in docs to the last stable (1.7.x / 2.2.x) via yarn.lock / constraints file to avoid breakage?

kyle: Yes — I'll make a tiny PR that updates package.json example to use "@redwood/sdk": "^2.2.4" and add a comment.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] job started: python-publish v1.8.0-canary (sha: abc123def) — publishing to testpypi. Logs: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/778/logs/42

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] command: `python -m build && twine upload --repository testpypi dist/*`

eva: Smoke runner: starting quick smoke suite now (embeddings, chat, streaming). Will post results in ~10m.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] publish step: SUCCESS for testpypi package v1.8.0-canary (sha: abc123def)

eva: Smoke results: embeddings test failing intermittently — 502 from runtime in 1/3 runs. stack: `ValueError: kv cache size mismatch at step 49`

sam: Hmm, that KV cache mismatch smells like a runtime mismatch between python client kv serialization and runtime patch we rolled last week. Not a packaging issue.

kyle: Given that, I'd avoid publishing TS canary until we know root cause. Options: A) rollback python release (yank canary tag on PyPI and delete testpypi artifact) B) keep canary but mark as unstable and proceed with local fix. Thoughts?

release-manager: Don't yank the release yet — it's testpypi canary only. But we need to block npm publish. We should: 1) tag this canary in the changelog as "smoke-failing" 2) hold TS publish 3) open a hotfix branch in python client and attempt reproducer + patch.

maya: Agreed. Let's hold TS. Kyle, can you add a short deprecation blurb for legacy sync client to the release notes draft? Something like: "Note: legacy sync client will be deprecated in 3 months; see migration guide link."

kyle: Will do. Draft snippet: "Deprecation: The legacy sync client (sync.* API) will be deprecated on 2026-07-10. Migrate to the async client or the new unified client — migration guide: https://docs.redwood/infer/migrate-sync-to-async"

sam: Also add a note in examples/ and README about pinning to the latest stable for production users. I'll PR that now.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] npm publish blocked: "release held by policy: failing smoke tests" — user: release-manager

npm-bot: Command suggestion: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.3.0-canary canary` (run after approval)

eva: Reproducer steps posted in the incident ticket: https://tickets.redwood/INC-9421 — includes minimal script to trigger kv mismatch.

kyle: Action items: 1) I will open hotfix branch and try to reproduce locally (assign to kyle) 2) Maya will update release notes w/ deprecation blurb + label current canary as unstable (assign to maya) 3) Sam will pin examples + PR (assign to sam) 4) Release-manager will block npm publish until smoke green (assign to release-manager)

release-manager: I'll also add an automated check: CI must pass smoke suite label `smoke:ok` before npm publish job proceeds.

maya: For rollback commands if we need them: 
```
# pypi yanking (if we decide to yank canary)
# twine doesn't "yank" — we'd remove dist and unpublish from TestPyPI UI
# For npm rollback (if already published):
npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk canary
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.2.4 latest
```

sam: Thanks — keeping TS blocked. Will monitor ticket.

eva: I'll re-run smoke with a diagnostic build (more logging) in ~15m and update here.

kyle: Fine plan. Please ping once smoke is green and then we can decide to promote to npm canary. Also we'll include the deprecation note in the release notes PR so docs and changelog are consistent. :thumbsup:

maya: Closing loop: no npm publish tonight. Python canary remains on TestPyPI for debugging only. Follow-up: hotfix attempt and status update by EOD PST.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] thread closed by release-manager (reason: hold ts publish)
